title: Modern History: National Movements (Past Year Questions)

questions.q_en: Which of the following groups/parties was started in San Francisco, United States of America, during the Indian National Movement?
questions.solution_en: The Ghadar Party was formed in San Francisco, USA, in 1913 by Indian revolutionaries such as Lala Hardayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, and Kartar Singh Sarabha. Its goal was to liberate India from British rule through an armed struggle.
questions.solution_hi: गदर पार्टी की स्थापना 1913 में लाला हरदयाल, सोहन सिंह भकना व करतार सिंह सराभा जैसे भारतीय क्रांतिकारियों ने अमेरिका के सैन फ्रांसिस्को में की थी। इसका लक्ष्य सशस्त्र संघर्ष के माध्यम से भारत को ब्रिटिश शासन से मुक्त कराना था।

questions.q_en: When was the Champaran Agrarian Law passed by the British Government?
questions.solution_en: The British Government enacted the Champaran Agrarian Law in 1918, prompted by Mahatma Gandhi's 1917 Champaran Satyagraha Movement. This movement sought to end the coercive cultivation of indigo on farmers' lands in the Champaran district.
questions.solution_hi: ब्रिटिश सरकार ने महात्मा गांधी के 1917 के चंपारण सत्याग्रह आंदोलन से प्रेरित होकर 1918 में चंपारण कृषि कानून पारित किया। इस आंदोलन का उद्देश्य चंपारण जिले में किसानों की भूमि पर नील की जबरन खेती समाप्त करना था।

questions.q_en: The Cabinet Mission came to India in_____ to discuss the ultimate transfer of power.
questions.solution_en: The Cabinet Mission arrived in India in 1946 with the purpose of discussing the modalities for the ultimate transfer of power from British rule to Indian hands. It played a crucial role in formulating proposals for the formation of a united and self-governing India, ultimately leading to the creation of the Mountbatten Plan and the subsequent partition in 1947.
questions.solution_hi: कैबिनेट मिशन 1946 में भारत आया, ब्रिटिश शासन से भारतीयों को अंतिम सत्ता हस्तांतरण की प्रक्रिया पर चर्चा करने के उद्देश्य से। इसने एक संयुक्त व स्वशासी भारत के गठन हेतु प्रस्ताव तैयार करने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई, जो अंततः माउंटबेटन योजना व उसके बाद के घटनाक्रम का आधार बना।

questions.q_en: Champaran Satyagraha was launched in which of the following years?
questions.solution_en: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was the first satyagraha movement led by Mahatma Gandhi in British India and is considered a historically important rebellion in the Indian independence movement. It was India's first Civil Disobedience movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi to protest against the injustice meted out to tenant farmers in the Champaran district of Bihar.
questions.solution_hi: 1917 का चंपारण सत्याग्रह महात्मा गांधी द्वारा ब्रिटिश भारत में शुरू किया गया पहला सत्याग्रह आंदोलन था और इसे भारतीय स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन में एक ऐतिहासिक रूप से महत्वपूर्ण विद्रोह माना जाता है। यह महात्मा गांधी द्वारा शुरू किया गया भारत का पहला सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन था, जो काश्तकार किसानों के साथ हो रहे अन्याय के विरोध में था।

questions.q_en: In which year was All-India Muslim League formed?
questions.solution_en: The All-India Muslim League was formed on December 30, 1906, in Dhaka. It was a political organization that aimed to represent the interests of Indian Muslims during the period of British colonial rule.
questions.solution_hi: अखिल भारतीय मुस्लिम लीग की स्थापना 30 दिसंबर, 1906 को ढाका में हुई। यह एक राजनीतिक संगठन था जिसका उद्देश्य ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन के दौरान भारतीय मुसलमानों के हितों का प्रतिनिधित्व करना था।

questions.q_en:
Which of the following organisations, divided into two branches, was established by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant?

Options:
questions.solution_en: The Home Rule League was established in 1916 by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant. It was divided into two branches - one led by Tilak in Maharashtra and Central Provinces, and another led by Annie Besant in the rest of India. The movement aimed at achieving self-government for India within the British Empire.
questions.solution_hi: होम रूल लीग की स्थापना 1916 में बाल गंगाधर तिलक व एनी बेसेंट ने की थी। यह दो शाखाओं में विभाजित थी - एक तिलक के नेतृत्व में महाराष्ट्र व मध्य प्रांतों में, और दूसरी एनी बेसेंट के नेतृत्व में बाकी भारत में। इस आंदोलन का उद्देश्य ब्रिटिश साम्राज्य के भीतर भारत हेतु स्वशासन प्राप्त करना था।

questions.q_en: Which important event that started in 1930 played a significant role in motivating and mobilizing Indians to join the nonviolent movement for independence?
questions.solution_en:
· The Salt Satyagraha (Dandi March), initiated by Mahatma Gandhi on March 12, 1930, was a pivotal event in India's freedom struggle.

· Gandhi and his followers marched 240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to protest the British salt tax, symbolizing defiance against colonial oppression.

· This nonviolent campaign mobilized millions of Indians, sparking widespread civil disobedience and uniting the nation against British rule.

Key Impact:

· The Salt Satyagraha globalized India's freedom struggle and solidified Gandhi's strategy of Satyagraha (nonviolent resistance).

Further information:

· Swadeshi Movement (1905 - 1911): Focused on boycotting British goods (pre-Gandhian era).

· Gadar Movement (1913s): A militant diaspora-led effort, not nonviolent.

· Quit India Movement (1942): Launched later, demanding immediate British withdrawal.
questions.solution_hi:
• 12 मार्च 1930 को महात्मा गांधी द्वारा शुरू किया गया नमक सत्याग्रह (दांडी मार्च), भारत के स्वतंत्रता संग्राम में एक महत्वपूर्ण घटना थी।

• गांधी व उनके अनुयायियों ने साबरमती आश्रम से दांडी तक 240 मील की पैदल यात्रा की, ताकि ब्रिटिश नमक कर के विरुद्ध विरोध जताया जा सके, जो औपनिवेशिक दमन के प्रति अवज्ञा का प्रतीक बना।

questions.q_en: Gandhiji hoped that by coupling non-cooperation with _________, India's two major religious Communities, Hindus and Muslims, could collectively bring an end to colonial rule.
questions.solution_en: Gandhiji envisioned that by aligning the non-cooperation movement with the Khilafat Movement, which aimed to protect the interests of Muslims regarding the Caliphate, Hindus and Muslims could unite in their struggle against colonial rule. This strategy aimed to foster Hindu-Muslim unity as a potent force against British imperialism.
questions.solution_hi: गांधीजी ने खिलाफत आंदोलन के साथ असहयोग को जोड़कर, जिसका उद्देश्य खिलाफत के संबंध में मुसलमानों के हितों की रक्षा करना था, यह कल्पना की कि हिंदू व मुसलमान औपनिवेशिक शासन के विरुद्ध अपने संघर्ष में एकजुट हो सकते हैं। इस रणनीति का उद्देश्य ब्रिटिश साम्राज्यवाद के विरुद्ध एक शक्तिशाली शक्ति के रूप में हिंदू-मुस्लिम एकता को बढ़ावा देना था।

questions.q_en: Who among the following signed the Poona pact with Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.solution_en: The Poona Pact was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar in 1932. It aimed to address the concerns of the depressed classes regarding political representation by ensuring separate electorates for them within reserved seats, as opposed to the Communal Award proposed by the British that would have granted them a fixed number of seats but without separate electorates.
questions.solution_hi: पूना पैक्ट पर महात्मा गांधी व डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर के बीच 1932 में हस्ताक्षर हुए। इसका उद्देश्य ब्रिटिश द्वारा प्रस्तावित सांप्रदायिक निर्णय (Communal Award) के विपरीत, दलित वर्गों को आरक्षित सीटों के भीतर पृथक निर्वाचिका सुनिश्चित कर राजनीतिक प्रतिनिधित्व संबंधी चिंताओं को संबोधित करना था।

questions.q_en: In which of the following years was the 'Quit India Movement' launched?
questions.solution_en:
· The Quit India Movement, also known as the August Movement or Bharat Chhodo Andolan, was a mass civil disobedience movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942 during World War II.

· It demanded an immediate end to British colonial rule in India.

· Gandhi gave the famous slogan "Do or Die" (Karo Ya Maro) to Indians, urging them to fight for complete independence.
questions.solution_hi:
• भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन, जिसे अगस्त आंदोलन भी कहा जाता है, महात्मा गांधी द्वारा द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के दौरान 8 अगस्त 1942 को शुरू किया गया एक व्यापक सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन था।

• इसने भारत में ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन के तत्काल अंत की माँग की।

questions.q_en: In which of the following cities did Mahatma Gandhi lead the peasant movement against the imposed indigo cultivation by the British planters?
questions.solution_en: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was Mahatma Gandhi's first major civil disobedience movement in India, where he fought against the exploitative indigo cultivation system imposed by British planters on local farmers.
questions.solution_hi: 1917 का चंपारण सत्याग्रह भारत में महात्मा गांधी का पहला बड़ा सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन था, जहाँ उन्होंने ब्रिटिश बागान मालिकों द्वारा स्थानीय किसानों पर थोपी गई शोषणकारी नील खेती प्रणाली के विरुद्ध संघर्ष किया।

questions.q_en: What was the name of the campaign led by the Ali brothers and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad to save the Ottoman Caliphate as a symbol of unity among the Muslim community?
questions.solution_en:
· The Khilafat Movement (1919 - 1924) was a pan-Islamic political protest campaign launched by the Ali brothers (Shaukat Ali and Mohammad Ali) along with Maulana Abul Kalam Azad and other leaders. Its aim was to pressure the British government to preserve the Ottoman Caliphate, which many Indian Muslims regarded as a symbol of Muslim unity and leadership.

· It also became a part of the larger Indian freedom struggle, and Mahatma Gandhi supported it as a unifying movement between Hindus and Muslims.

· It eventually merged with the Non-Cooperation Movement led by Gandhi.

Further information:

Wahabi Movement

· Timeframe: 1820s onwards

· Leader: Syed Ahmed Barelvi

· Objective: To revive Islamic principles and purify Islam by removing un-Islamic practices; later turned into a militant movement against British rule.

Ahmadiya Movement

· Timeframe: Late 19th century

· Founder: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad

· Objective: Reform Islamic practices, promote peace, rational thinking, and oppose religious violence.

Faraizi Movement

· Timeframe: 1830s

· Founder: Haji Shariatullah

· Objective: To reform Muslim society by focusing on religious duties (Faraiz) and removing un-Islamic customs.

· Region: Bengal

· Later Leader: Dudu Miyan, who gave it a more anti-landlord and anti-British character.

· Significance: It was both a religious reform and socio-political movement.
questions.solution_hi: • खिलाफत आंदोलन (1919-1924) अली बंधुओं (शौकत अली व मोहम्मद अली) व मौलाना अबुल कलाम आजाद तथा अन्य नेताओं द्वारा शुरू किया गया एक पैन-इस्लामिक राजनीतिक विरोध अभियान था। इसका उद्देश्य ब्रिटिश सरकार पर ऑटोमन खिलाफत को संरक्षित रखने हेतु दबाव डालना था, जिसे कई भारतीय मुसलमान महत्वपूर्ण मानते थे।

questions.q_en: The campaign 'Ek Tareekh, Ek Ghanta, Ek Sath' is associated with which occasion?
questions.solution_en:
• This campaign promotes cleanliness and was launched on Gandhi Jayanti.

• Full Name: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi

• Born: 2 October 1869, Porbandar, Gujarat

• Died: 30 January 1948, New Delhi

• Education: Studied law in England; later went to South Africa, where he began his political activism.

• Satyagraha: Gandhi's philosophy of non-violent resistance, first practiced in South Africa and later in India.

• Champaran Movement (1917): First successful Satyagraha in India, supporting indigo farmers in Bihar.

• Kheda Satyagraha (1918): Protested against tax collection during famine conditions.

• Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22): Urged Indians to boycott British institutions.

• Civil Disobedience Movement (1930): Launched with the Dandi March, breaking the salt law.

• Quit India Movement (1942): A mass protest demanding an end to British rule, launched with the slogan "Do or Die".

• Role in Partition: Advocated Hindu-Muslim unity and opposed the partition of India.

• Death: Assassinated by Nathuram Godse on 30 January 1948.
questions.solution_hi:
• यह अभियान स्वच्छता को बढ़ावा देता है और गांधी जयंती पर शुरू किया गया था।

• पूरा नाम: मोहनदास करमचंद गांधी

• जन्म: 2 अक्टूबर 1869, पोरबंदर, गुजरात

• मृत्यु: 30 जनवरी 1948, नई दिल्ली

• शिक्षा: इंग्लैंड में कानून का अध्ययन किया; बाद में दक्षिण अफ्रीका गए, जहाँ उन्होंने अपनी राजनीतिक सक्रियता शुरू की।

questions.q_en: Due to which of the following events did Rabindranath Tagore return the title of 'Knighthood' to the British Government while expressing his anguish?
questions.solution_en:
Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919, where British troops under General Dyer killed hundreds of unarmed Indians.

• Option 1: Charan Paduka Incident - Not related.

• Option 2: Partition of Bengal - Happened in 1905; no connection with knighthood.

• Option 4: Chauri Chaura Incident - Led to Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement withdrawal but was not linked to Tagore's knighthood.
questions.solution_hi:
रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर ने 1919 के जलियाँवाला बाग हत्याकांड, जिसमें जनरल डायर के अधीन ब्रिटिश सेना ने सैकड़ों निहत्थे भारतीयों को मार डाला, के विरोध में अपनी नाइटहुड की उपाधि त्याग दी।

• विकल्प 1: चरण पादुका घटना - संबंधित नहीं।

• विकल्प 2: बंगाल का विभाजन - 1905 में हुआ; नाइटहुड से कोई संबंध नहीं।

questions.q_en: With which of the following organisations was Lala Har Dayal associated?
questions.solution_en:
Lala Hardayal started the Ghadar movement in the early twentieth century among Indians in North America, primarily Sikhs, to end British rule in their country of India. On July 15, 1913, the Ghadar Party was founded in Astoria, Oregon.

He founded the Ghadar Party in the United States. This party's members were expatriates who wanted to start an international movement against British rule in India. On July 15, 1913, the Ghadar Party was founded in Astoria, Oregon.
questions.solution_hi: लाला हरदयाल ने उत्तरी अमेरिका में भारतीयों, मुख्यतः सिखों, के बीच बीसवीं सदी की शुरुआत में गदर आंदोलन शुरू किया, ताकि उनके देश भारत में ब्रिटिश शासन समाप्त हो सके। 15 जुलाई 1913 को, एस्टोरिया, ओरेगन में गदर पार्टी की स्थापना हुई। उन्होंने संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका में गदर पार्टी की स्थापना की।

questions.q_en: The Non-Cooperation Movement was called off after which of the following incidents?
options_en: Outbreak of the First World War
questions.solution_en:
The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-1922) was led by Mahatma Gandhi to resist British rule through non-violent means. However, it was called off after the Chauri-Chaura incident in February 1922, where a violent clash between protestors and police resulted in the burning of a police station and the death of 22 policemen. Gandhi, emphasizing non-violence, withdrew the movement following this event.

Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.
questions.solution_hi: असहयोग आंदोलन (1920-1922) का नेतृत्व महात्मा गांधी ने अहिंसक तरीकों से ब्रिटिश शासन का विरोध करने हेतु किया था। हालाँकि, फरवरी 1922 में चौरी-चौरा घटना के बाद इसे वापस ले लिया गया, जिसमें प्रदर्शनकारियों व पुलिस के बीच हिंसक झड़प के कारण एक पुलिस थाने में आग लगा दी गई व 22 पुलिसकर्मियों की मृत्यु हो गई।

questions.q_en: The Hindu Mahasabha was founded as a response to Muslim fundamentalism in which year?
questions.solution_en: The Hindu Mahasabha was established in 1915 as a reaction to rising concerns about Muslim fundamentalism and political activism during that period. It aimed to advocate for Hindu interests and promote Hindu nationalism as a response to perceived threats to Hindu identity and culture.
questions.solution_hi: हिंदू महासभा की स्थापना 1915 में उस समय बढ़ती मुस्लिम कट्टरता व राजनीतिक सक्रियता संबंधी चिंताओं की प्रतिक्रिया के रूप में हुई। इसका उद्देश्य हिंदू हितों की वकालत करना व हिंदू पहचान व संस्कृति को कथित खतरों की प्रतिक्रिया में हिंदू राष्ट्रवाद को बढ़ावा देना था।

questions.q_en: Khudai Khidmatgars, a non-violent movement among the Pathans, was started by ______.
questions.solution_en: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, also known as Frontier Gandhi, founded the Khudai Khidmatgars (Servants of God) movement. It was a non-violent resistance movement against British rule, primarily active in Northwest Frontier Province (now in Pakistan).
questions.solution_hi: खान अब्दुल गफ्फार खान, जिन्हें सीमांत गांधी भी कहा जाता है, ने खुदाई खिदमतगार (ईश्वर के सेवक) आंदोलन की स्थापना की। यह ब्रिटिश शासन के विरुद्ध एक अहिंसक प्रतिरोध आंदोलन था, जो मुख्यतः वायव्य सीमा प्रांत (अब पाकिस्तान में) में सक्रिय था।

questions.q_en: After the _______, Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.
questions.solution_en: The Chauri Chaura incident occurred at Chauri Chaura in the Gorakhpur district of the United Province, (modern Uttar Pradesh) in British India on 4 February 1922, when a large group of protesters, participating in the Non-cooperation movement, clashed with police, who opened fire. In retaliation the demonstrators attacked and set fire to a police station, killing all of its occupants. The incident led to the deaths of three civilians and 23 policemen. Mahatma Gandhi, who was strictly against violence, halted the Non-cooperation Movement on the national level on 12 February 1922, as a direct result of this incident.
questions.solution_hi: चौरी चौरा घटना 4 फरवरी 1922 को संयुक्त प्रांत (वर्तमान उत्तर प्रदेश) के गोरखपुर जिले के चौरी चौरा में हुई, जब असहयोग आंदोलन में भाग ले रहे प्रदर्शनकारियों का एक बड़ा समूह पुलिस से भिड़ गया, जिसने गोली चला दी। इसके प्रतिशोध में प्रदर्शनकारियों ने हमला कर आग लगा दी।

questions.q_en: Which Act opposed by Mahatma Gandhi in 1919 was a direct attack on the civil liberties and democratic rights of the Indian people?
questions.solution_en:
· The Rowlatt Act of 1919 allowed the British government to imprison people without trial.

· Gandhi launched the Rowlatt Satyagraha in protest.

· The Rowlatt Act (officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act) was passed in March 1919 by the Imperial Legislative Council.

· It authorized the British government to imprison people without trial, restrict civil liberties, and conduct trials without juries.

· Gandhi strongly opposed this act and launched a non-violent protest movement against it.

· This opposition eventually led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in April 1919, when British troops fired on unarmed protesters in Amritsar, killing hundreds of people.
